contentBlocks.text: This week you wrote a full argumentative piece. Let's review it all!

Quick review: a strong claim is specific, debatable, and defensible (Day 1). Facts, expert opinions, and examples are three evidence types (Day 2). A counterclaim and rebuttal address the other side (Day 3). All five pieces assemble into one complete argument (Day 4). Read your finished argument aloud, and point out which sentence is your claim, your strongest evidence, and your counterclaim.
Wonderful work this week — you wrote a real, complete argumentative piece with claim, evidence, and a counterclaim! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review claim criteria, evidence types, counterclaim/rebuttal, and full argument structure
Identify the claim, strongest evidence, and counterclaim within the child's own finished argument
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child read their finished argument aloud.
3. Have the child point to and label the claim, strongest evidence, and counterclaim.
4. Complete the review worksheet.
5. Celebrate finishing a full week of argumentative writing!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on correctly identifying just the claim and counterclaim, the two clearest 'position' pieces, before the evidence
Ready for more: ask the child to read their argument to a family member and explain what each part does
This is a good checkpoint to note whether the child needs more practice on claims, evidence, or counterclaims before the next argumentative-writing unit
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a recall and self-identification activity — check that the child can correctly point out their own claim, strongest evidence, and counterclaim within their finished Day-4 argument.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Grade 6 Writing standard W.6.1a-e work before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.

generationData.instructions: Answer each question to review this week.

rows.problem: Name your strongest piece of evidence.
